title: KV slab smoothener and evictor rate shaper with tenant reservation windows
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring fragmentation spikes and short-lived allocation storms from tenant burst traffic which cause reactive spillover to local NVMe and cascading eviction storms. Those spill/eviction bursts increase p99 latency for inference requests and create noisy neighbor effects on shared Dedicated pools. This PR introduces a combined allocator + eviction control strategy to smooth slab-level free space, pace eviction throughput, and provide soft per-tenant reservation windows to reduce spillovers.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Implements a slab 'smoothener' that migrates small free runs between slabs to reduce fragmentation, introduces an eviction-rate shaper that caps eviction throughput and ramps it based on measured IO/backpressure, and adds tenant-aware short-term reservation windows so active tenants get a stable allocation when under transient bursts. Also includes telemetry, unit and perf tests, and a staged rollout plan.

Design notes: - Slab smoothener: background task that periodically samples slab free-run histograms and executes low-cost free-run coalesces (move/merge) for slabs whose fragmentation score exceeds a threshold. Moves are sized to fit into existing allocation slack and avoid large temporary memory spikes. The task supports a configurable 'aggressiveness' parameter and an idle-only mode to avoid interference with hot allocation paths. - Evictor rate shaper: instead of instantly trying to evict to satisfy a memory shortfall, the shaper enforces an eviction budget (evictions/sec and io_bytes/sec) and uses a PID-inspired controller to ramp up/down eviction throughput based on measured spill queue depth and disk latency. This prevents eviction-induced I/O storms and gives the smoothener time to reclaim space. - Tenant reservation windows: ephemeral soft reservations per-tenant that allocate a small buffer of tokens proportional to recent allocation rate. The reservation is reclaimable but lowers the chance of an otherwise healthy tenant being victim to an eviction wave. Reservation behaviour is tunable by tenant tier. - Continuous batching interplay: added a coordination hook so the batch scheduler can signal expected short-term allocation needs; the smoothener defers aggressive moves if a large batch is in flight to avoid extra copying.

Operational controls and knobs: configuration variables added to src/kv/config.rs (smoothener.enabled, smoothener.aggressiveness, evictor.rate_limit, evictor.io_budget_bytes_per_sec, tenant.reservation_window_ms, reservation.tier_multipliers). Default values are conservative for canary rollout.

Benchmarks: synthetic tenant burst test (100 tenants, 20% heavy bursts) measured on perf-lab: - fragmentation_score (median) down 35% - spill-to-disk events down 18% - steady-state memory overhead +1.8% (due to reservation slack) - p99 latency for 512-token generation decreased by 7% under burst conditions

Rollout plan: 1) Canary on 'redwood-dedicated-canary' (5% capacity) with smoothener.idle_only=true and evictor.rate_limit conservative; 2) Monitor metrics: kv.fragmentation_score, kv.eviction_rate, kv.spill_count, tenant.alloc_stalls; 3) Increase aggressiveness after 72h stable canary; 4) Gradual 25/50/100% ramp with automated rollback on spike in spill_count or p99.

Notes on safety: All background moves are no-copy where possible (relink free-run descriptors) or bounded-copy with atomic handover to avoid corrupting the KV index. Evictor shaper maintains a small emergency bypass for OOM-critical paths.

review_thread: Michael Lang: Can we quantify the CPU cost of the smoothener at default aggressiveness? Priya Kapoor: Measured ~2-3% CPU at canary fleet on perf-lab under normal load; it's configurable and default is idle_only which reduces CPU. Diego Chen: The move code touches allocation paths — how do you ensure we don't introduce races with concurrent allocations? Priya Kapoor: Smoothener acquires per-slab lightweight epoch pin and uses compare-and-swap handover for descriptors; added unit tests that stress concurrent alloc/free. Sana Patel: We saw a flaky test in evictor unit tests on first CI run (race on io_budget reset) — please add guard and retry. Priya Kapoor: Fixed in commit 4, added deterministic sleep in the test to reproduce; re-ran CI. Michael Lang: LGTM after Diego's nit on error logging; Diego Chen: Approved with comment to include a structured log field 'kv.smoothener.move_reason'. Merge was blocked until the flaky test was stabilized and perf run passed. Final PR author reply: thanks — addressed comments, tightened timeouts, and added additional perf assertions.

One rerun required for evictor_test.rs (race) which passed after fix. All checks green before merge.

release_notes:
Improves KV memory fragmentation and reduces eviction/spill bursts: adds slab smoothener (background defragmentation), eviction-rate shaper (backpressure-aware eviction pacing), and tenant soft reservation windows. Metrics: kv.fragmentation_score, kv.eviction_rate, kv.spill_count. Configurable knobs under KvConfig.

Impact: Should reduce p99 latency during tenant bursts and lower disk spill events. Conservative defaults enabled for canary rollout.
notes_for_oncall: If rollout causes increase in kv.spill_count or sustained eviction_rate above configured io_budget, disable smoothener.aggressiveness or evictor.rate_limit via remote flags and rollback; emergency bypass exists to free memory but will increase spill events. Monitor disk latency and tenant.alloc_stalls.
footnotes: This PR intentionally favors safety over aggressive reclamation for initial rollout. Future follow-ups: 1) adaptive aggressiveness based on workload type, 2) kernel-level async move support for zero-copy relocations, 3) per-model reservation tuning.
